newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia home loans more afforable - survey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia home loans more afforable - survey.

text.p: Australians can meet the costs of home loan repayments more easily than at any time in the last two years, according to an industry survey released on Monday.

The Citibank/Real Estate Institute of Australia Home Loan Affordability Indicator showed home loan affordability rose 5.3 percent in the December quarter and was 12.3 percent higher than at the same time last year.

"While rising house prices around Australia pushed up the size of the average loan, interest rate cuts by the Reserve Bank (of Australia) resulted in a 3.5 percent decrease in average loan repayments during the December quarter," the survey said.
"Combined with a 1.6 percent increase in median family income, it is significantly easier for people to meet mortgage repayments."
It said the December quarter rise continued the steady climb which began in the September quarter 1995.
Affordability is measured as the fraction of the average income needed to pay the average new home loan.

The survey calculated that Australians now used an average 25.2 percent of their income for loan repayments, compared to 26.6 percent in the September quarter 1996 and 28.7 percent at this time last year.

Citibank senior economist Annette Beacher said further large gains in home loan affordability depended on the RBA's future interest rate decisions and the maintenance of the high degree of competition in the mortgage market.

"Household incomes will improve over the course of this year as there are gathering signs of strengthening employment growth and high levels of job vacancies throughout Australia," Beacher said in a statement.

"Despite the RBA being unlikely to cut interest rates again, further increases in home loan affordability are also possible with greater mortgage competition amongst the banks and other financial institutions," she said.
